title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1966-05-19
source: Set 1 Source: sbd > 10 inch Master Reels @ 15 ips 1/2 track > Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with good instrument separation but noise‑reduced drums that sound backwards; early Bear work shines despite the missing second set.
ai_review.review: The SIR Mick release captures a clear first‑set soundboard mix where Jerry’s early playing is evident, especially on “Beat It On Down The Line.” However, aggressive noise reduction has warped the drum image, making them sound reversed and detracting from an otherwise solid tape. The second set is absent, limiting the overall concert experience.

ai_rating.rationale: One detailed review gives a middling 3‑star score; the performance is decent but incomplete and the recording suffers from noticeable drum processing issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Good instrument separation, but noise reduction applied to drums creates a backward‑sounding effect; vocals have slight echo, overall resonance weaker than comparable release #106828.

standout_songs: Beat It On Down The Line
show_quality.setlist_flow: Only the first set is present; reviewers note the missing second set which includes several classics.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Early‑era playing noted with good instrument clarity, no specific praise beyond that.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob's (Bobby) vocals described as having a slight echo due to the recording treatment.
band_member_comments.Drums: Criticized for sounding backwards because of noise reduction processing.
